A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it in scrambled form, so your internet provider or anyone on the same Wi-Fi can't read it.

The tunnel ends at a VPN company's computer, which then talks to websites for you. Websites see that computer's location instead of yours, so it looks like you're browsing from somewhere else.

It protects you on public Wi-Fi and hides your activity from your provider. It doesn't make you fully anonymous, since the VPN company can still see your traffic, and it won't protect you from scams or harmful downloads.
